messages.content:
You are a senior hedge-fund analyst filing statements into a library of open questions about NVIDIA and its world. For each statement, return the ids of the questions it is filed under, or an empty list. Read each question's 'takes' line: it says what that question collects. A statement filed under no question is a valid answer, not a failure: never file a statement under a question it does not bear on because no better question exists.
File each statement under the narrowest question that names its matter, and under that one only; never add a broader question beside it. A company-wide figure question (total revenue, segment revenue, gross margin, operating margin, profit, capex) takes only the company's own reported figures, guidance, estimates of that figure and management's statements about it. News about a customer, supplier, competitor, product, policy or deal is filed under the question that names that matter (an event, a policy process, a theme), or under none when no question names it. A rumour is filed exactly as a confirmed statement is.

[Item] the-decoder.com, 2026-07-06: Nvidia's Kyber NVL144 reportedly pushed back more than a year, Asian suppliers drop

[Open questions]
  - v1 (NVDA, due 2027-02-28): How much will NVIDIA’s disclosed commitments for guarantees and similar obligations to cloud providers reach in its FY2027 annual filing?
      takes: financing_amount figures, guidance, estimates and revisions for NVIDIA commitments and guarantees to cloud providers over 2026-02-01..2027-01-31, and the direct drivers of that figure stated with a size; statements about the matter 'NVIDIA cloud-provider financing and capacity partnerships' (also called AI Compute Partnership, DSX AI Factory, AI Compute Partnership Program, Firmus, Sharon AI, Lambda): NVIDIA’s financial guarantees, capacity-purchase commitments, leasebacks, and revenue-sharing arrangements with cloud providers and data-center customers. belong here under any of those names
  - v2 (NVDA, due 2027-12-31): Will NVIDIA sign or announce a financial guarantee for OpenAI’s Ohio data-center lease by 2027-12-31?
      takes: the terms, amounts, counterparties, agreements and approvals of this obligation or deal, and its steps, confirmations and denials: OpenAI Ohio data-center lease guarantee; statements about the matter 'NVIDIA cloud-provider financing and capacity partnerships' (also called AI Compute Partnership, DSX AI Factory, AI Compute Partnership Program, Firmus, Sharon AI, Lambda): NVIDIA’s financial guarantees, capacity-purchase commitments, leasebacks, and revenue-sharing arrangements with cloud providers and data-center customers. belong here under any of those names
  - v3 (NVDA, due 2027-02-24): How much financing and other commitment exposure will Nvidia report for its AI-cloud customer backstop arrangements at the FY2027 annual filing?
      takes: financing_amount figures, guidance, estimates and revisions for AI-cloud customer backstop arrangements over 2026-02-01..2027-01-31, and the direct drivers of that figure stated with a size; statements about the matter 'NVIDIA cloud-provider financing and capacity partnerships' (also called AI Compute Partnership, DSX AI Factory, AI Compute Partnership Program, Firmus, Sharon AI, Lambda): NVIDIA’s financial guarantees, capacity-purchase commitments, leasebacks, and revenue-sharing arrangements with cloud providers and data-center customers. belong here under any of those names
  - v4 (NVDA, due 2027-02-28): What will Nvidia's total revenue be in FY2027?
      takes: total_revenue figures, guidance, estimates and revisions for Nvidia total revenue in FY2027 over 2026-02-01..2027-01-31, and the direct drivers of that figure stated with a size
  - v5 (NVDA, due 2026-12-31): Will Nvidia begin shipping Vera Rubin by December 31, 2026?
      takes: steps, dates, delays, confirmations and denials of this event, and named customers' statements about receiving it: Rubin; statements about the matter 'Vera Rubin rollout' (also called Vera Rubin, Rubin): Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform production and shipment rollout. belong here under any of those names
  - v6 (chip-export-controls, due 2027-01-31): Will Chinese authorities permit Nvidia H200 chips to be sold in China by the end of FY2027?
      takes: the decisions, drafts, approvals, denials and deadlines of this process, and any statement of whether and how much the permitted or restricted activity is actually happening: Chinese permission for Nvidia H200 sales in China; statements about the matter 'H200 China sales and export controls' (also called H200, H200 China sales, China export controls): U.S. export-control clearance and Chinese market access for Nvidia H200 chips belong here under any of those names
  - v7 (NVDA, due 2027-02-28): At NVIDIA's next annual filing, how much credit-support obligation will NVIDIA have taken on through its AI compute framework?
      takes: financing_amount figures, guidance, estimates and revisions for AI compute framework credit-support obligations over 2026-02-01..2027-01-31, and the direct drivers of that figure stated with a size; statements about the matter 'NVIDIA cloud-provider financing and capacity partnerships' (also called AI Compute Partnership, DSX AI Factory, AI Compute Partnership Program, Firmus, Sharon AI, Lambda): NVIDIA’s financial guarantees, capacity-purchase commitments, leasebacks, and revenue-sharing arrangements with cloud providers and data-center customers. belong here under any of those names
  - v10 (NVDA, due 2027-02-28): What will Nvidia's total revenue growth be in FY2027?
      takes: growth_rate figures, guidance, estimates and revisions for Total revenue over 2026-02-01..2027-01-31, and the direct drivers of that figure stated with a size
  - v8 (ai-capex, due 2027-03-31): How much will the big four AI hyperscalers spend in total on data center capital expenditures in calendar 2026?
      takes: spend_total figures, guidance, estimates and revisions for Data center capital expenditures by the big four AI hyperscalers over 2026-01-01..2026-12-31, including estimates for another population or wording of the same aggregate, and the direct drivers of that figure stated with a size; statements about the matter 'AI hyperscaler data center capital spending' (also called AI capex, data center capital expenditures, big four AI hyperscalers): The combined annual data center capital expenditures of the big four AI hyperscalers and forecasts of that aggregate. belong here under any of those names
  - v9 (ai-capex, due 2028-03-31): How much will the big four AI hyperscalers spend in total on data center capital expenditures in calendar 2027?
      takes: spend_total figures, guidance, estimates and revisions for Data center capital expenditures by the big four AI hyperscalers over 2027-01-01..2027-12-31, including estimates for another population or wording of the same aggregate, and the direct drivers of that figure stated with a size; statements about the matter 'AI hyperscaler data center capital spending' (also called AI capex, data center capital expenditures, big four AI hyperscalers): The combined annual data center capital expenditures of the big four AI hyperscalers and forecasts of that aggregate. belong here under any of those names
  - v11 (NVDA, due 2027-12-31): Will Nvidia launch the Kyber NVL144 rack architecture by 2027-12-31?
      takes: steps, dates, delays, confirmations and denials of this event, and named customers' statements about receiving it: Kyber NVL144 rack architecture; statements about the matter 'Kyber NVL144 rollout' (also called Kyber, Kyber NVL144, NVL144, PCB midplane): Development and launch timing of Nvidia's Kyber NVL144 rack architecture, including reported manufacturing challenges with its PCB midplane. belong here under any of those names
  - v12 (NVDA, due 2027-02-28): How much stand-alone CPU revenue will Nvidia report for FY2027?
      takes: product_revenue figures, guidance, estimates and revisions for stand-alone CPU over 2026-02-01..2027-01-31, and the direct drivers of that figure stated with a size
  - v13 (NVDA, due 2028-12-31): Will Nvidia launch the Kyber rack architecture by 2028-12-31?
      takes: steps, dates, delays, confirmations and denials of this event, and named customers' statements about receiving it: Kyber; statements about the matter 'Kyber NVL144 rollout' (also called Kyber, Kyber NVL144, NVL144, PCB midplane): Development and launch timing of Nvidia's Kyber NVL144 rack architecture, including reported manufacturing challenges with its PCB midplane. belong here under any of those names
  - v14 (NVDA, due 2027-02-24): What will NVIDIA report for Data Center segment revenue in FY2027?
      takes: segment_revenue figures, guidance, estimates and revisions for Data Center over 2026-02-01..2027-01-31, and the direct drivers of that figure stated with a size
  - v15 (NVDA, due 2027-02-28): How much will NVIDIA's supply commitments reach in its FY2027 annual filing?
      takes: financing_amount figures, guidance, estimates and revisions for supply commitments over 2026-02-01..2027-01-31, and the direct drivers of that figure stated with a size; statements about the matter 'NVIDIA supply commitments': NVIDIA's supplier commitments and their disclosed amount belong here under any of those names
  - v16 (chip-export-controls, due 2027-01-31): By January 31, 2027, will an official decision in the Valar Atomics, Texas, and Utah litigation affirm the NRC’s authority to license the microreactors at issue?
      takes: the decisions, drafts, approvals, denials and deadlines of this process, and any statement of whether and how much the permitted or restricted activity is actually happening: NRC licensing authority over the microreactors at issue in the Valar Atomics, Texas, and Utah litigation; statements about the matter 'US microreactor licensing authority litigation' (also called Valar Atomics microreactor litigation, NRC microreactor licensing authority): Litigation involving Valar Atomics, Texas, and Utah over whether the NRC has authority to license some microreactors. belong here under any of those names

[Statements]
  - e1 [rumour] who: SemiAnalysis | SemiAnalysis reported that Nvidia's Kyber NVL144 rack was delayed by more than 12 months, to 2028, due to manufacturing problems. | quote: Asian tech stocks slid after analyst firm SemiAnalysis reported on X that Nvidia's next AI server rack system, Kyber NVL144, has been pushed back more than twelve months to 2028 because of manufacturing problems.
  - e2 [rumour] who: SemiAnalysis | SemiAnalysis said the Kyber NVL144 PCB midplane was difficult to manufacture without defects. | quote: Specifically, the PCB midplane, a central board that connects all the individual components, has proven extremely difficult to produce without defects.
  - e3 [rumour] who: SemiAnalysis | SemiAnalysis reported that Nvidia scrapped its planned NVL72x2 design, which would have placed two Oberon racks back to back. | quote: A planned alternative design called NVL72x2, which would have placed two Oberon racks back to back, has been scrapped entirely.
  - e4 [rumour] who: SemiAnalysis | SemiAnalysis reported that cloud providers and large data center operators objected to the NVL72x2 form factor and operational overhead. | quote: Cloud providers and large data center operators pushed back against the unusual form factor and the high operational overhead.
  - e5 [rumour] who: SemiAnalysis | SemiAnalysis reported that Nvidia canceled the Rubin Ultra version with four compute dies. | quote: The more powerful version of the upcoming Rubin Ultra chip with four compute dies has also been canceled.
  - e6 [rumour] who: SemiAnalysis | SemiAnalysis reported that only the two-die Rubin Ultra version remains and delivers roughly half the real-world compute performance of the canceled version. | quote: Only the smaller two-die version remains, delivering roughly half the real-world compute performance.
  - e7 [rumour] who: SemiAnalysis | SemiAnalysis reported that CPO-NVSwitch will not arrive until Nvidia's Feynman generation, the generation after next. | quote: A key interconnect technology called CPO-NVSwitch, which links many chips into a single large system, won't arrive until the generation after next, called Feynman.
  - e8 [rumour] who: The Decoder | The report said Nvidia plans to sell more Oberon-Rubin racks in the existing form factor to make up for the shortfall. | quote: Nvidia plans to make up for the shortfall by selling more Oberon-Rubin racks in the existing form factor.

Return one placement per statement id, in order.

Why did you return no links for e3 about the cancelled NVL72x2 design? Which exact original instruction and source statements did you rely on? Which two alternative interpretations did you reject, and why? Consider the whole request, and separate what was shown from what you inferred.
